title: service-automation: a suspended run resumes on the flow version it started on, not on the definition registered under its name
body:
epic:#28130#1 · hotlong · session_040dfd80c4c9411b895c698e785a6848

Filing gate: ④ child of epic #28236 (P1, cut after ADR-0146's rewrite merged in #28295); Q3 ruled 「四个小问题 同意」: flow customization waits for real version pinning, no interim publish gate. ⛔ Not a claim.

Part of #28236 (P1, child **N-12**) · governs: ADR-0146 D9 item 4, amends ADR-0009 (resume reading of `executionPinned`) · lane: `domain:server` (`packages/services/service-automation`) · size: M.

**Business reason.** An approval or screen step can wait for days. If the flow is republished meanwhile, today the waiting run continues on the new definition, or is killed when its step was renamed. A customer must be able to change a flow without breaking the runs already in flight; that is the precondition for every flow customization (N-11, N-18).

**Measured (`75ecaf4ad8`).**
- `service-automation/src/run-resume.ts#resolveResumeTarget` reads `flows.get(run.flowName)` (HEAD) and answers a cause when `run.nodeId` is missing; `settleUnresumableSuspension` turns it into `RUN_NOT_FOUND`.
- `SuspendedRun.flowVersion` (`engine.ts:1657`) and `sys_automation_run.flow_version` (`sys-automation-run.object.ts:154`) hold `FlowSchema.version` (`spec/src/automation/flow.zod.ts:1082`, an author integer, default `1`) — not a content identity: two bodies can carry the same number.
- `engine.ts:2774` `flowVersionHistory` is in-process and lost on restart.
- `metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts#getByHash` resolves a body by `(type, name, checksum)` from `sys_metadata_history`, and history GC skips pinned types; nothing in `service-automation/src` calls it.
- A code-loaded body has no history row; the loader's registered body is the only copy (not verified for an upgraded package).

**Wanted.**
1. A run records, at start, a content identity of the definition it started on (the checksum `sys_metadata_history` keys by, or an equal hash of a code-loaded body), persisted on the suspended-run row. `flow_version` stays as display.
2. `resolveResumeTarget` resolves the pinned body first: the armed definition if its identity matches; else `getByHash`; else a loaded code body with that identity. The resume finishes on it; new runs start on the armed definition.
3. A row with no recorded identity (written before this card) keeps today's reading.
4. A pinned body that cannot be recovered anywhere (a code package upgraded under the run) keeps today's reading (HEAD, node checked) and logs a `warn` naming the version it could not recover. ⛔ Never a silent HEAD resume when the pinned body exists. *Decided here where D9 is silent; the PR states it.*
5. The pre-flight (`unresumableSuspensionCause`) and the resume still classify through the one function.

**Tests.** A run suspended on v1 and resumed after v2 renames its node finishes on v1 (re-judges `unresumable-suspension-cause.test.ts`: no longer `RUN_NOT_FOUND`). A body changed without a `version` bump is still pinned. The pin survives an engine restart (durable store). A legacy row resumes on HEAD. An unrecoverable code body warns and resumes on HEAD. New runs after v2 use v2.

**Not here.** The flow override and its rebinding (N-11); Studio "Customize this flow" (N-18); recording code bodies in history (ADR-0009 §2.4 keeps the triple-only rule).

**Dedupe.** Related, not duplicates: #23963 (closed; unresumable run left `paused`), #11665 (closed; the clone-to-customize design this replaces). Searched `executionPinned`, `resume version`, `resume RUN_NOT_FOUND node`, `suspended run definition changed`: no open card pins the resume.

Links back: #28236, ADR-0146 D9, ADR-0009 §2.1/§2.2, ADR-0126 §2.
